We have crystallized a bifunctional isomerase/decarboxylase enzyme and determined its molecular weight and the space group of its crystal.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the structure of the bifunctional enzyme 2-hydroxymethyl-2,4-hepta-2, 4-diene-1,7-dioic acid isomerase/ 5-oxo-2,5-pentadiene-1,3,5-tricaboxylic acid decarboxylate.
the crystallization, preliminary X-ray analysis and structure determination of this bifunctional enzyme from E. coli.
the elucidation of the three-dimensional structure of a bifunctionl enzyme which catalyses the last two steps in a pathway for the degradation of a lignin model compound.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystals contain a tetramer in a crystal lattice with a cell dimension of 106 X 127 X 139 A, which is consistent with the V(m) value.
the enzyme crystallizes as a tetramer in space group P2 (1)2 (1) 2 (1) with a single molecule of the cofactor, FMN, in the asymmetric unit.
the enzyme is a tetramer with a molecular weight of 178 060 Da in the crystal lattice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this enzyme is the first bifunctional enzyme of a degradation pathway for which the crystal structure has been determined.
we have crystallized a bifunctional protein which is a tetramer in solution, but forms a dimer in the crystal.
we have crystallized a bifunctional protein and have obtained a preliminary data set to 3.2 A resolution which will be used to determine its structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it provides a new example of a protein that can be crystallized from an aqueous solution without the use of additives.
the enzyme is not a monomer in solution and that the tetrameric state of the protein is the biologically active form.
the use of PEGs in crystallization is not always the best option and that the choice of precipitant is important.
